title: Superconducting Pairing Symmetry on Geometric-Algebra Foundations via the Scalar-Projection Method
abstract: We formulate the low-energy theory of superconducting pairing in the geometric algebra $Cl_{3,0}$. Conventional BCS mean-field theory and its extensions ($s$-, $p$-, $d$-wave, etc.) have algebraic counterparts in an eight-dimensional real multivector space. The construction is a two-level projection: matrix blocks are represented as Clifford multivectors, and their grade-0 projected geometric products extract the scalar blocks from which Hamiltonians are built. The result is an algebraic reconstruction, physically equivalent to the standard complex-matrix formulation. In this reconstruction, the dichotomy of pairing channels acquires an algebraic root: it follows from the fermionic identity $B^\dagger(V)=-B^\dagger(V^{\mathsf T})$, and the Fierz rearrangement is realized by the map $Φ:G\mapsto Ge_{31}$ (with $e_{31}^2=-1$). This yields a kernel/matrix dictionary: at the effective-kernel level grades $0\oplus3$ correspond to spin singlets and grades $1\oplus2$ to triplets; at the pairing-matrix level the singlet plane is $\mathrm{span}\{e_2,e_{31}\}$. The BCS limit has a double grade identity: kernel grade 0 (scalar glue) and vertex grade 2, a bivector ($iσ_2\leftrightarrow e_{31}$). We state three algebraic results: (i) a decomposition theorem for BdG quantum geometry with a null-texture criterion, applied to the chiral-state controversy in CsV$_3$Sb$_5$; (ii) a Fierz sign duality in the four-dimensional Minkowski algebra, with a chirality-reversal extension to two-node Weyl-semimetal models; (iii) an error bound and condition-number structure for tomographic reconstruction under a linear-response probe model. Illustrations include a glue-generation mechanism, a one-loop algebraic renormalization flow whose feeding constant coincides in magnitude with the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ Casimir, closed-form $μ=0$ inter-node spectra, and a UTe$_2$ two-phase analysis.
summary: This paper develops a highly abstract, yet powerful, algebraic framework for describing superconducting pairing symmetry using Geometric Algebra. It reformulates standard BCS theory by projecting complex matrix structures into scalar Hamiltonians via a scalar-projection method. The work yields fundamental algebraic theorems applicable to diagnosing superconducting phases and topological properties in correlated materials.
main_problem: The paper aims to formulate the low-energy theory of superconducting pairing symmetry using a novel algebraic framework.
main_result: It establishes an algebraic reconstruction of pairing theory using Geometric Algebra, yielding specific theorems regarding BdG quantum geometry and Fierz sign duality.
method: The core method is the Scalar-Projection Method applied within the framework of Geometric Algebra (Cl_{3,0}), projecting complex matrix blocks onto scalar Hamiltonians.
model_or_system: The theory applies to superconducting pairing in various materials (e.g., UTe2, CsV3Sb5) and models, drawing parallels to BCS theory and heavy-fermion systems.
key_observables: Gap matrices (E1, O1, etc.), anomalous correlators, and the superconducting order parameter ($\Delta_0$).
important_parameters: The pairing symmetry channels (singlet/triplet), the Fermi surface topology, and the gap-equation self-consistency condition.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on specific algebraic identities (e.g., fermionic identity) and assumes certain minimal node structures for chirality-reversal theorems.
figures_summary: The notes mention tables comparing the framework to Landau theory and derivations for four gap matrices (E1, O1, O3, O2, O4) leading to energy eigenvalues.
paper_structure: The paper is highly structured, moving from the general algebraic formulation (Clifford algebra, scalar projection) to specific physical results: decomposition theorems for BdG geometry, Fierz duality in Minkowski algebra, and detailed model analyses for specific superconductors (UTe2, Weyl semimetals).
why_interesting: While focused on superconductivity, the rigorous algebraic machinery (Clifford algebra, projection methods) provides a powerful, unified mathematical language applicable to other strongly correlated systems where symmetry constraints are paramount.
